newsitem.title: UK: British Energy job cuts slammed by union.
newsitem.headline: British Energy job cuts slammed by union.

text.p: The nuclear industry's largest union slammed British Energy's proposed job cuts on Wednesday as "a kick in the face" and vowed there would be no compulsory redundancies.

In a statement responding to British Energy's announcement that it would seek 1,460 redundancies in the next three years, the Amalgamated Engineering and Electrical Union (AEEU) said the company would have to justify every job cut.
AEEU spokesman Danny Carrigan said in a statement trade unions would be raising concerns over safety within the company after the job losses.
But he expressed relief that British Energy had not decided to close company offices at Edinburgh, Gloucester or East Kilbride and that there were no plans to close power stations.
"It appears our behind the scenes lobbying has helped keep all three offices open," he said in a statement.

British Energy had earlier said the job cuts should lead to annual savings of 50 million stg in staff costs and that it would take a one-off restructuring charge of 100 million stg, fully covered by existing provisions, over three years.
